facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Discovery of shock-metamorphosed material establishes the impact origin of Lonar Crater.
facts.text: Lonar Crater was formed by a hypervelocity meteorite impact into the Deccan basalt plateau in the Buldhana district of Maharashtra.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: National Geological Monuments of India. Designated, 1979.
facts.text: The Geological Survey of India designated the Lonar impact crater as a National Geological Monument in 1979.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The crater measures 1.8 km (1.1 mi) in diameter and is 150 m (490 ft) deep.
facts.text: The rim-to-rim diameter of the Lonar impact structure measures approximately 1.8 kilometres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Coarse breccia with shatter coning and microbreccia with moderately shocked fragments containing maskelynite were found in drill holes through the crater floor.
facts.text: Core drilling by Fredriksson and colleagues verified the impact origin of Lonar by identifying plagioclase converted to shock-produced maskelynite.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: While earlier analyses dated the structure to 52 ± 6 ka, subsequent argon-argon dating ( 40Ar/ 39Ar) yielded a much older age of 570 ± 47 ka. However, the 40Ar/ 39Ar age has been disputed, as inherited argon in the samples may have resulted in an overestimation of the crater's age.
facts.text: The exact age of the Lonar impact remains disputed between thermoluminescence dating yielding about 52,000 years and argon-argon dating yielding about 570,000 years.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Change in colour was due to a salt-loving bacteria (red-coloured archaeal strains classified as halophilic archaea or haloarchaea). It is associated with high salinity and alkalinity (pH).
facts.text: Microbial investigations by the Agharkar Research Institute confirmed that Lonar Lake's rapid color transition to pink in June 2020 was caused by a bloom of Haloarchaea.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The lake is saline and alkaline, with pH levels soaring to around 10.5, which are among the uncommon values in most natural lakes.
facts.text: The water of Lonar Lake maintains exceptional alkalinity and salinity, reaching a pH level of approximately 10.5 during periods of high evaporation.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Ramsar Wetland. Designated, 22 July 2020. Reference no. 2441.
facts.text: Lonar Lake was officially recognized as a wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention in July 2020.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Henry Cousens dates the temple to the end of the 13th and beginning of the 14th centuries CE. He is of the opinion that the construction of the temple was never completed due to invasions of the Delhi Sultanate.
facts.text: The Daitya Sudan Temple in Lonar town was recorded by Archaeological Survey of India scholar Henry Cousens as an incomplete Hemadpanthi-style basalt temple from the 13th to early 14th century CE.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The legend associated with the temple states that a giant named Lonasura (or Lavanasura) used to reside in the area... Therefore, the Daitya Sudan (giant-slayer) incarnation of Vishnu is worshipped here.
facts.text: The Lonar Mahatmya of the Skanda Purana describes the manifestation of Vishnu as Daitya Sudan to defeat the subterranean asura Lonasura.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: This Lake was first mentioned in Skanda Purana, Padma Purana and the Aaina-i-Akbari.
facts.text: The Padma Purana describes Lonar as a sanctified water tirtha linked to the destruction of the demon's underground stronghold.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: The Lonar lake is supposed to be the pit within which the giant had resided, with its water representing his blood. A nearby hill is supposed to be the lid which Vishnu had thrown open.
facts.text: Local folklore tells that the lake itself was the subterranean den of the demon Lonasura, and that its saline and tinted waters represent his shed blood.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: the legend that the idol in the temple is an actual fragment of the meteorite itself and has magnetic properties
facts.text: Popular local belief maintains that the sacred idol in Lonar's Mota Maruti temple was carved out of a magnetic fragment of the fallen meteorite.

sheet.summary: According to the Skanda Purana and local lore, the circular crater formed when Vishnu took the Daitya Sudan avatar to break open the subterranean lair of the demon Lonasura. Geological surveys confirmed that the depression is actually a 1.8-kilometre-wide hypervelocity meteorite crater in basalt, while biological studies proved the lake's sudden pink coloration in June 2020 resulted from a bloom of salt-loving Haloarchaea. Geochronologists sharply disagree on the impact's timing, debating whether it struck 52,000 years ago based on thermoluminescence or 570,000 years ago based on argon-argon isotope measurements. It remains unknown whether inherited argon skewed the older radiometric dates, leaving the true age and precise composition of the extraterrestrial impactor an open scientific question.
